concepts.def: Uprising triggered by Bloody Sunday massacre; forced Tsar Nicholas II to issue October Manifesto promising Duma.
Strikes and mutinies in Petrograd forced Nicholas II to abdicate; Provisional Government took power.
Bolshevik seizure of power in Petrograd led by Lenin and Trotsky; stormed Winter Palace, overthrew Provisional Government.
1918-21 policy nationalising industry and forcibly requisitioning grain to win Civil War; caused mass famine.
New Economic Policy under Lenin allowing small private trade and ending grain requisitioning; restored agricultural output.
Stalin's industrialisation programme from 1928; rapid heavy industry growth at huge human cost in gulags.

walkthroughs.body_html:
Russia 1914-41 — a core area of A-Level History.

Working through it builds the schema you need: the key terms, how they connect, and how to use them together.

Russia 1914-41 brings together several ideas you need to use as a set, not in isolation.

Lock in the vocabulary first, then practise pulling the ideas together to answer real questions.

Use the activities in this adventure to build familiarity with Russia 1914-41.

Practise vocabulary, calculations and free-text questions to lock in the learning.

mcqs.q: Who led the Bolsheviks in October 1917?
options: Stalin
Lenin
Kerensky
Trotsky
Five-Year Plan
Collectivisation
NEP
Perestroika
The 1905 Revolution achieved nothing because the Tsar stayed in power.
The 1905 Revolution was led by Lenin from the Winter Palace.
It failed to overthrow the Tsar but forced the October Manifesto creating the Duma, exposing autocracy's weaknesses and rehearsing the structures of 1917.
The NEP was introduced by Stalin to fund the Five-Year Plans.

mcqs.q: Why did Lenin introduce the NEP in 1921?
options: The NEP was introduced by Stalin to fund the Five-Year Plans.
War Communism had collapsed the economy and provoked the Kronstadt revolt; the NEP allowed limited private trade to restore production and stabilise Bolshevik rule.
The Schlieffen Plan failed because it tried to invade Russia first.
The NEP was Lenin's plan to permanently switch Russia to capitalism.
